keyword: when does artemis 2 return to earth

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to return to Earth on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA’s Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down... on Friday, April 10." (R1); "set for Friday, April 10" (R2); "Friday, April 10" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state splashdown/return on Friday, April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splash down off the coast of San Diego" (R1); "off the coast of San Diego" (R2); "Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported by NASA and other sources specifying location.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission splashdown is targeted for approximately 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)" (R1); "around 8:07 p.m. (5:07 p.m. PDT)" (R2); "around 8:07 p.m. ET" (R3)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission crew will be recovered by helicopter.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "deliver them to the USS John P. Murtha" (R1); "flown to the USS John P. Murtha" (R2); "USS John P. Murtha" (R3)

verifications.claim: The vehicle for the Artemis II mission return is the Orion Spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: During Artemis II mission reentry, the crew will experience high temperatures up to 5,000°F (2,760°C).
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: "temperatures of about 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit" (R1); "3,000-degrees Fahrenheit" (R3); "nearly 5,000F (2,760C)" (R6); "2,760 degrees Celsius (5,000 degrees Fahrenheit)" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: NASA sources (R1,R3) state 3,000°F; others (R6,R8) state 5,000°F/2,760°C, creating contradiction.

verifications.claim: During Artemis II mission reentry, the crew will travel at nearly 25,000 mph (40,230 kph).
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.reasoning: Sources vary (23k-25k mph); 'nearly 25,000' broadly supported but not precise in all, especially NASA R2 lower.
